description: Make a fist with your thumb pressed up against the side of your index finger, knuckles facing forward.
practice_tip: Keep your thumb tight against the fist — a loose thumb starts to look like S.

description: Extend all four fingers straight up and together, with your thumb folded across your palm.
practice_tip: Fingers should be together and vertical; watch that your thumb stays tucked, not poking out.

description: Curve your fingers and thumb to form a C shape, like holding an invisible cup, thumb opposite the fingertips.
practice_tip: Imagine holding a tennis ball — the C should be rounded, not squared off.

description: Point your index finger straight up while the other fingers and thumb form a small circle touching the thumb.
practice_tip: The circle made by the middle finger and thumb should sit right behind the upright index finger.

description: Curl all four fingers down so the fingertips rest near the thumb, forming a closed claw shape.
practice_tip: Think of a loose fist with visible fingertips — don't tuck the fingers all the way in.

description: Touch your index finger and thumb together to form a small circle, with the other three fingers extended upward.
practice_tip: It's like an 'OK' hand flipped upright — keep the three back fingers straight and together.

description: Point your thumb and index finger forward, parallel to each other and horizontal, like a pinch pointing sideways.
practice_tip: G points sideways (like G in the alphabet points 'sideways'); keep the two digits close together.

description: Extend your index and middle fingers together, pointing sideways horizontally, thumb tucked over the folded fingers.
practice_tip: Same two fingers as U, but rotated to point sideways — a common beginner mix-up with U and G.

description: Extend only your pinky finger straight up; fold the other fingers down with your thumb across them.
practice_tip: Keep the pinky isolated and upright — it's the easiest letter to learn and a good anchor.

description: Start like the letter I (pinky up) and trace a J shape in the air with your pinky — down, then curving to the side.
practice_tip: J is I plus motion. In this trainer we show the static handshape; practice the J-trace separately.

description: Hold your index and middle fingers up in a V, with your thumb pressed between them at the base of the V.
practice_tip: The thumb peeking between the two fingers is what separates K from V — make it visible.

description: Extend your index finger up and your thumb out to the side, forming an L shape; fold the other fingers.
practice_tip: Literally trace the letter L with your thumb and index — palm orientation should face forward.

description: Fold your fingers over your thumb so the thumb tip hides under the ring finger area, three fingers draped over the thumb.
practice_tip: The thumb tucks under three fingers for M but only two for N — count the fingers over the thumb.

description: Fold your fingers over your thumb so the thumb tip hides under the middle finger area, two fingers draped over the thumb.
practice_tip: Same family as M, S, and T — the difference is exactly where the thumb sits under the fingers.

description: Curve all fingers and the thumb so the fingertips meet the thumb tip, forming a round O shape.
practice_tip: Close the ring fully — a gap at the top turns O into C for a fast reader.

description: Make the K handshape (V with thumb between) but point it downward/sideways, wrist angled so the fingers aim down.
practice_tip: P is K tipped forward — identical fingers, different wrist angle. Drill them back to back.

description: Make the G handshape (thumb and index parallel) but point it downward, like a pinch aimed at the floor.
practice_tip: Q is G tipped forward — same pinch, different direction. Another wrist-angle pair with G.

description: Cross your middle finger over your index finger while both point up, other fingers folded, thumb tucked.
practice_tip: The crossing is the whole letter — make sure the fingers visibly overlap, not just touch.

description: Make a fist with your thumb laid across the front of your curled fingers, knuckles facing forward.
practice_tip: Contrast with A: in A the thumb hugs the side, in S it lies across the front of the fingers.

description: Make a fist with your thumb tucked between your index and middle fingers, the thumb tip poking out.
practice_tip: Look for the thumb tip peeking between the two fingers — that peek is the signature of T.

description: Extend your index and middle fingers straight up and pressed together, other fingers folded, thumb tucked.
practice_tip: U and V are siblings: fingers together = U, fingers apart = V. Drill them as a pair.

description: Extend your index and middle fingers up in a V shape, spread apart, other fingers folded, thumb tucked.
practice_tip: Think 'victory' sign — the spread between the fingers should be obvious at a glance.

description: Extend your index, middle, and ring fingers up and spread slightly to form a W, thumb across the folded pinky.
practice_tip: Three fingers up with visible gaps — if the gaps close, W starts to read as a blurry U.

description: Hook your index finger into a bent, claw-like curve while the other fingers stay folded, thumb across them.
practice_tip: X is like a fishhook — the index should be clearly bent, not straight like D or folded like S.

description: Extend your thumb and pinky out to the sides like a 'hang loose' sign, folding the middle fingers down.
practice_tip: Stretch the thumb and pinky wide — the wide span is what makes Y instantly readable.

description: Point your index finger up (like D without the circle) and trace a Z in the air — across, diagonal, across.
practice_tip: Z is D-plus-motion, like J is I-plus-motion. Practice the Z-trace slowly, then build speed.
